hook: Harvey's floodwater was waist deep. The Army sent trucks.
narration: They had to wade out through Harvey's floodwater to reach an Army truck.
This was Katy, Texas, outside Houston, at the end of August 2017.
Texas Army National Guard soldiers drove the flooded streets looking for anyone stranded.
Tall military trucks like these can drive through water that would stall a car.
Soldiers carried bags on their shoulders and walked people back through the water.
Then they pulled each person up into the back of the truck.
Five thousand Guard soldiers were working around Houston, and seven thousand more were on the way.
outcome: The truck carried them out of the flood to dry ground.
title: Army trucks wade into Harvey's flood
question_comment: Would you have waded out, or waited for the water to drop?

facts.claim: Guard soldiers drove Katy streets rescuing stranded residents
facts.source_quote: Soldiers from the Texas Army National Guard drive the streets of Katy, Texas rescuing residents who are stranded by the flood.
The Soldiers are part of the 5,000 that are currently working in and around the Houston area as part of the response to Hurricane Harvey.
7,000 more Texas National Guard Soldiers are mobilizing and will be deployed to the affected areas as needed.

description:
Texas Army National Guard soldiers drove the flooded streets of Katy, Texas, rescuing residents stranded by Hurricane Harvey in August 2017.
